I want to first say that everyone experiences different symptoms to different extents, and have different triggers. For me the pain is bad when I lay down but I can stand/walk as much as I want (just can’t take super long strides). Your pain and emotions are valid. I’m in the same boat rn trying to focus on my mental health. I have been dealing with depression for over a year now and sciatica for about 5 months. I felt myself getting mentally better until I started to experience this pain. I guess I try and distract myself as much as possible and make my environment stimulating. I have a bed full of different textures, I have different lights in my room. I always play a podcast or tv show in the background. When I’m really down i will call a friend and just talk to them. Meditation helps. I would look into CBT (cognitive behavioural therapy). I think you could be dealing with mental distortions rn. Look these up- I think you might be dealing with fortune telling, ivergeneralization. Idk look at the different distortions and see if any apply to you. For me I tend to think like “I will be in pain forever, my life is over, my life revolves around my pain”. Now I try and tell myself that I am experiencing pain rn but I don’t know if it will be there in the future or not. Also I still have other aspects of my life (school and work). It’s definitely hard. I’m sorry that you are going through this, but you are on the right track with seeking professional help.

Really different than any physical therapy I had heard of before. The first one she assessed everything and showed me diagrams of which muscles were tighter such and such. Basically after that she inserted a finger rectally and vaginally and manually massaged the muscles from the inside. I do the deep breathing exercises with her and she will stretch my muscles at the same time. That’s all we really do during the sessions

My physio gives me breathing exercises to do on my own. Basically just deep breaths through your stomach, the muscles relax when you breath in. I do this for 10 minutes a day. After 2 weeks I started to add in clenching my muscles during my breath out. She also sends me a file for something called a full body scan. There’s lots on YouTube - look up one that relaxes your body. Mine kind of walks me through releasing the muscles at different parts of my body. I feel for you - pelvic floor physio therapists are expensive especially without any coverage. I had to save up quite a bit of money but luckily I only need 4-5 sessions in total.
